The nsys kernel activity table carries durations, not DRAM/SM throughput, so per-kernel memory traffic remains unknown pending separate counter-based profiling of candidates.
unavailable_fields.python_runtime.clean_latency_score: cProfile perturbs host dispatch; its inclusive/self times include host waits and are neither clean latency_ms scores nor GPU compute durations. Clean latency comes only from the harness measurement (torch.cuda.synchronize-bracketed perf_counter_ns, infer.py:53-58); these fields are diagnostic host-cost evidence only.
unavailable_fields.device_telemetry.per_forward_utilization: Not selected: NVML utilization is a device-wide sampled active fraction with device-dependent native periods that cannot attribute a sub-millisecond 15-kernel forward; the nsys per-kernel intervals and gaps provide the precise busy/idle decomposition this objective needs.

plan.rationale: Objective is latency_ms of one full graph-encoder forward on a single GPU (wall clock around infer() with torch.cuda.synchronize on both sides, infer.py:53-58), i.e. host dispatch plus launch plus kernel time for 15 sequential small FP32 kernels. Trace evidence: torch already ran (coverage.json: 15 cuda_kernels, 15 associated, 0 unassociated, 0 autograd ranges, 0 ambiguous forward sequences), so op-to-kernel attribution is complete and torch is not re-selected; the forward is plain eager PyTorch with no CUDA graphs, so node-level graph tracing is not required. Capability evidence: observations.json marks communication not_applicable ('single-device task'), which rules out nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and any communication-dimension field; device_telemetry only adds device-wide NVML rates/utilization that cannot attribute this GPU-resident, sub-millisecond forward; candidate_diagnostics has no candidate bundles in this revision. The two open latency questions are (1) how measured wall time decomposes into per-kernel GPU busy time versus inter-kernel idle/launch gaps on the expected single stream, and (2) how much host dispatch/binding cost the ~15 tiny op submissions incur. nsys is available (request.json tools.nsys, 2025.3.1) and resolves (1) with a separately run, cudaProfilerApi-bounded, low-perturbation capture providing nanosecond per-kernel start/end, demangled names, deviceId/streamId and memcpy/memset rows, with GPU counters left off; python_runtime resolves (2) with a warmed cProfile ranking host self/cumulative costs (diagnostic only, never a score). execution_timeline is not selected: its distinctive outputs (c10d CPU-submission linkage, gradient post-accumulate callbacks, cross-rank clock bounds) are inert for single-rank inference and its per-device gap/sync intervals would duplicate the nsys decomposition at higher profiler perturbation.
